0.0.n: 戦車道 names the fictional martial art of tank combat; 道 adds the idea of a disciplined practice.

0.1.n: に marks the pursuit to which the girls devote their youth.

0.2.n: Refers to their youthful years and energy, rather than young people.

0.3.n: を marks 青春 as what the girls devote.

0.4.n: 懸ける suggests committing something precious wholeheartedly; here it describes the girls before 女子高生.

0.5.n: Combines 女子, female students, with 高生, a shortened form referring to high school students.

0.6.n: たち attaches to 女子高生 to explicitly indicate a group.

0.7.n: を marks the girls as the people depicted by the work.

0.8.n: Past form of 描く, used before the title to describe what the work portrays.

0.11.n: An English loanword forming part of the title ガールズ＆パンツァー.

0.13.n: A German loanword meaning tank, forming part of the title ガールズ＆パンツァー.

1.0.n: Used figuratively to evoke the tank fighters’ toughness and armored vehicles.

1.1.n: の links 鉄 to 乙女, creating the descriptive phrase iron maidens.

1.2.n: A literary word for young women, giving the girls a dramatic description.

1.3.n: たち makes 乙女 explicitly refer to multiple young women.

1.4.n: の connects the maidens to their final battle.

1.5.n: 最後 combines with の to describe 戦い as the last one.

1.6.n: の lets 最後 describe the following noun 戦い.

1.7.n: The noun related to 戦う, to fight; here it refers to the girls’ final contest.

1.8.n: が marks the final battle as what will begin in the next line.

1.10.n: 全 means all or total, and 話 counts episodes.

1.11.n: の connects the episode count to the series it describes.

1.12.n: Strengthens 新作 to emphasize that the production is entirely new.

1.13.n: Describes newly made content, rather than reused material.

1.14.n: OVA is an abbreviation for animation originally produced for video release.

1.15.n: An English loanword referring to the connected set of episodes.

1.16.n: として marks the format in which the final battle will be presented.

2.0.n: この directly modifies the following noun 冬.

2.1.n: この冬 gives the time of the event without needing a following particle.

2.3.n: Emphasizes anticipation as the long-awaited beginning approaches.

2.4.n: Polite form of 始まる; the future timing comes from この冬 and the announcement context.

0.lit: Girls & Panzer, which depicted high school girls who devote their youth to the way of the tank.
0.tip: Japanese puts descriptions before nouns: everything through 描いた describes the title that follows.

1.lit: The iron maidens’ final battle, as a completely new OVA series of six episodes in total,
1.tip: This line leaves the sentence unfinished; が marks the subject of 始まります in the next line.

2.lit: This winter, at last, will begin!
2.tip: 始まります means something begins, not that someone starts something.
